what: Hirschkorn's key, note 52 of a Boston GP-178 grand, on his printed frame (Hirschkorn 2004, Appendix A): his key's printed points and lines, its outline traced from his Figure A.1 where his tables give no number, its mass, center of mass and inertia from Table A.1, its bushings from Table A.9, and his dip target. His frame bears on the key where his model does, at Pg4 and Pg5, but on real felts: a flat front punching washer over Pg4, and a flat back rail cloth strip lying wholly under the tail's chamfer, its rounded front edge over Pg5, each with its top where his round of 5 mm has its, since what is drawn is what is touched. The key, nose-up at rest, bears on the cloth's front edge, 0.06 mm from where it bears on his round. His printed frame on his rounds lets the key fall 9.306 mm at Pk2, where his finger presses; on the real felts 9.308 mm, 1.7 µm more, from the curvature of his rounds and the printed length of Pk5's normal (tools/derivations/11-hirschkorn-key-outline.py). His keybed, rails, papers, pins and the key's width are not published: they are those of the owner's measured section (data/profiles/measured-section.json), so his key height is an indication. It arrives as his frame is printed, not regulated: his dip of 10.0 mm is one regulation away.

key_kind.why: His Figure A.1 draws a natural: a covering whose lip overhangs a key front.

key_mass.why: Table A.1 gives the key's mass, its center of mass in the key's frame and its inertia, weighed and located on the key itself, leads in it: the statics read them as published, the height of the center of mass included. The figure's CMk marker stands elsewhere; Table A.1 governs.

arrival.why: On his printed frame as it is printed: the felts' tops where his rounds' tops stand, which no regulation laid. His dip of 10.0 mm is a target of his regulation, which the printed frame does not meet.

values.rule: Over his front bearing, where the front rail pin stands: the key front's 237.80 mm less Pg4's 217.2 mm = 20.6 mm.
values.why: His tables give no front mortise. Borrowed from the owner's key as a slot sized not to bind on his geometry: placed over his front bearing, the owner's length and depth, its top about 0.9 mm above the borrowed front rail pin at the bottom of the stroke, so that the pin never stops the key.
Not published. Assumed as the measured section's is: three times the balance pin's 3.4 mm diameter (key-frame-sections.json, balance_pin_diameter), 10.2 mm, the proportion of the owner's sketch.

Not published. Assumed: about a tenth of the keystick's height, the proportion of the owner's sketch, where the balance hole is drilled. Not measured.

Not published. Assumed as the measured section's is: half his key button's 6.21 mm height, 3.105 mm, the proportion of the owner's sketch; the slot is bushed in its upper part only (balance-mortise.json, construction).

His Figure A.1 draws no clearance for the wippen rail between the capstan and the back check block, the key coming back to its full height behind it: it draws the key's top lowered from just behind the capstan all the way to the key's end, and his key is kept as he drew it (tail_length).

values.rule: From the key's end to where the keystick's full height ends behind the capstan, both traced (hirschkorn-key-outline.json): full_height_back's -132.45 mm less tail_end's -233.52 mm = 101.07 mm.
values.why: His Figure A.1 draws the keystick at its full height from the key front to just behind the capstan, and its top lowered from there to the key's end, the back check block glued on the lowered part: that lowered part is the thinned tail, and the capstan screws into the full height. The full height's top over its last 29.65 mm, behind a line the figure draws down the wood 102.79 mm behind the pin, is drawn 0.75 mm above the keystick's full height (stick_height): within the trace's uncertainty, up to 1.62 mm at its markers, so it is dropped, and the full height is the keystick's one height. Nothing touches that stretch of the top, and the capstan's top is Pk3's, printed, whatever its seat.
His figure draws no felt on the key's tail, and his model has no damper.

values.why: His back bearing is printed as a round, which a flat cloth strip replaces with its top where the round's top is.

Borrowed from the frame of the owner's measured section: a shape, not a setting. The key rests on the cloth's front edge, which this radius rounds about a center over Pg5's x: the chamfer, 0.72 degrees from the cloth's face at rest, passes over that center the radius times (1/cos 0.72 degrees - 1) above the face, 0.04 µm, so that doubling the radius moves the rest by a fifth of a microradian.

values.rule: The cloth's front edge over Pg5's x, where his back round bears, the strip lying behind it: Pg5's -203.7 mm less the cloth's half-length of 12.0 mm = -215.7 mm.
values.why: His back bearing is printed as a round, which a flat cloth strip replaces with its top where the round's top is. The borrowed 24 mm strip lies wholly under the tail's chamfer, its front edge where his round bears, so that the key, nose-up at rest, rests on that edge where his model rests. The owner's account: most grand keys rest on an edge like this one, and it hardly matters for regulating, which sets the key's height with papers under the balance punching; what matters is that the cloth damps the key's return and that the key comes back to the same rest. A key bedded flat on its cloth wears it more slowly than one resting on an edge.
Not published. Borrowed from the frame of the owner's measured section. Drawn, and read by nothing else.

Not published. Borrowed from the frame of the owner's measured section, as the rest of his frame is: on his key, 24.02 mm high under a key button of 6.21 mm, on the same punching, it stands 2.77 mm above the key button, where the owner states a pin stands.

values.why: A rail section holds a pin's height whether or not the rail has a pin.

values.rule: No punching sits on the back rail: its cloth does.

values.rule: Naturals and sharps meet the back rail's cloth at one place: the rail has one row.
values.why: A rail section holds the offset between its two rows of pins whether or not it has two.

No key height is published: his regulation sets the dip and the hammer's height, not the key's. The target is the key height his key stands at on its frame as it arrives, so regulating it lays the dip and leaves the key height where it stands.
